subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should repeated byte-identical exec auto-reviewer inputs be memoized within a reviewer instance, and what security-relevant fields must be in the cache key?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but changing exec approval cache semantics affects a security boundary and existing labels already require maintainer review/product direction.

options.title: Memoize full reviewer input per instance
options.body: Cache allow and ask decisions for the lifetime of the model-backed reviewer using the complete ExecAutoReviewInput so repeated byte-identical approval misses do not re-bill completions.

options.title: Memoize only allows with tighter TTL
options.body: Reuse only low-risk allow-once verdicts for a short in-memory window, reducing cost while keeping deferrals and failures uncached.

options.title: Keep current per-call review
options.body: Preserve the current security posture and accept repeated model cost for identical approval misses.

recommendation.title: Memoize full reviewer input per instance
recommendation.body: Cache allow and ask decisions for the lifetime of the model-backed reviewer using the complete ExecAutoReviewInput so repeated byte-identical approval misses do not re-bill completions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex/exec reviewer trust and routing work makes this the strongest available owner for the approval-boundary decision.
